graphEvents.label: Which single-executor steps are enforced by code rather than prose
Why a fan-out lineage runs all its iterations in one process
Fan-out policy is prose keyed on flag shape; fanout-run never re-checks lineage count
Fan-out path excludes phase_init and phase_main_loop by design
In-process iteration is a deliberate CLI-lineage design that contradicts the fresh-context principle
Timestamp anomaly telemetry exists but is explicitly advisory
Every hard check is called only from inside a YAML step
verify-iteration passes when packet-level phases never ran
No script asserts run completion; config status has no asserting reader

label: The fan-out policy lives only in the command doc and presentation asset, keyed on flag shape; fanout-run.cjs spawns whatever lineage list it receives with no minimum count and no comparison against that policy, so a one-entry config JSON reaches the fan-out path while the caller believes it selected the runner for the single-executor path.

The fan-out path does not skip phase_init as an error; it is defined without it. The YAML instructs a jump directly to phase_synthesis, skipping phase_init and phase_main_loop entirely for every lineage count, and the child prompt re-asks for those phases in prose with nothing outside the child noticing whether it complied.

In-process iteration is a deliberate CLI-lineage design: the child prompt states THIS process is the executor for EVERY iteration and that the YAML's per-iteration dispatch steps are already satisfied, with the code comment giving the cause (nested dispatch is denied inside the sandbox, so a literal leaf burns every iteration on dispatch failures). This overrides the YAML operating principle and the mode skill's fresh-context core innovation without naming the exception in either.

The signal that would have exposed the incident already exists and is recorded as advisory only: checkLineageTimestampWindow compares each state record timestamp against the lineage dispatch window, a timestamp_anomaly row is written to the status ledger and folded into orchestration-summary.json, but the comment states timestamp telemetry cannot affect lineage fulfillment and the exit code is computed from fulfilled/rejected alone.

Every hard check in the loop is invoked from inside a YAML step (gateway append, verify-iteration, loop-lock, synthesis-closeout invariants), so a route that skips the workflow skips all of them at once; this is the structural reason the incident produced no failure in any existing check.

verify-iteration.cjs passes on a run whose packet-level phases never happened: it asserts narrative, delta, per-iteration state record and gateway receipt inside the given artifact dir, and never asserts a lock, session classification, spec check, synthesis writeback, continuity save or config completion; route proof degrades to a warning.

No script asserts that a run completed. step_update_config_status writes status complete as the workflow's own completion marker, yet the only reader of that field in the runtime scripts is readStoredLineageSessionId, which uses it solely to decide whether to reuse a session id, so the incident's third run stayed initialized with nothing objecting.

fanout-run.cjs is the shared lineage executor for research, review and ai-council (the council orchestrate-session.cjs calls it and the prompt/skill paths are parameterised by loop type), so a reporting change in that one file reaches all three modes while a per-mode compliance check would have to be built three times.
A check can only catch a route that skips a workflow if the check has a caller outside that workflow.
A runner's status ok or succeeded is a verdict about the process, not about the workflow the process was supposed to follow.

direction: Treating the 2539-line workflow YAML as the enforcement layer
reason: No YAML step validates that phase_init or phase_save actually ran; its checks fire only for a session already walking its steps.

direction: Treating the packet lock as the detector for a non-workflow run
reason: A run that never calls loop-lock.cjs leaves no contention to observe; absence of a lock is not an observable the current code tests.

direction: Treating fanout-merge status ok as a workflow verdict
reason: It is a merge verdict emitted unconditionally once the registry writes succeed; refusals cover reducer provenance only.

direction: Expecting validate.sh to catch the skipped phases
reason: It validates packet document structure, which a skipped phase_init leaves untouched and therefore valid.

direction: Looking for a packet-level phase receipt analogous to dispatch-receipts
reason: Receipts exist per iteration dispatch inside the lineage only; there is no phase receipt to assert against.
